# Introduction

- Question: do local income taxes cause workers to move their residence?
  - Treatment: a municipality's EIT resident-rate change. Outcome: whether workers live where they work.
- Setting: PA EIT, levied at the residence — the tax follows the worker home. LODES block-level OD, 2002–2019.
- Hook: the max-rule T = max(muni + SD, nonresident) splits identical increases into a binding treatment and a non-binding placebo.
- Headline: a binding increase cuts live-and-work workers by about 10% (-0.437 per pp, marginal with property controls). Placebo null.
- Credibility: within-design placebo; clean muni-level pre-trend; dCDH reproduces sign and pre-trends.
- Property tax: competing burden, enters as a control.
- Contributions:
  - Built-in placebo from the max-rule.
  - Live-and-work measured directly from LODES.
  - Causal evidence a residence-based tax moves residence; revenue consequence quantified.
- Roadmap.

# Background

- Enabling laws (chronological):
  - Sterling Act (1932): Philadelphia wage tax.
  - Act 511 (1965): authorizes the local EIT; 0.5% muni + 0.5% SD cap.
  - Act 47 (1987) and Home Rule: the only routes above the cap.
  - Act 1 (2006): SDs may shift property tax onto the EIT; anti-windfall rules.
  - Act 32 (2008, effective 2012): consolidated withholding via county TCDs — the enforcement shock.
- The max-rule: T = max(muni + SD, nonresident). Home stack vs work-side rate; the larger sets the bill.
- Data producers: DCED (rate register, AFR); STEB (common-level ratios); Census F-33 / NCES (SD finance). TCDs are the collection mechanism, not a dataset.
- Property tax (control, not treatment):
  - Muni, SD, and county millage on assessed value; STEB certifies the CLR per county, annually.
  - Infrequent reassessment (24/67 counties) + Act 1 anti-windfall → statutory millage ≠ burden.
  - Use the effective rate (millage x CLR) per layer.
  - Attaches to the dwelling, not the worker.

Exhibits:

- Figure `law_timeline` — PA local-tax statutes.
  - Say: the laws create and constrain the variation; Act 32 makes the EIT bind.

# Empirical Framework

## The causal parameter

- Estimand: the ACR — dose-weighted average per-pp effect; the regression beta.
  - ACRT(d): marginal-effect curve. ATT(d): total effect at dose d.
- Identifying assumptions:
  - Strong parallel trends — parallel across dose magnitudes (Callaway, Goodman-Bacon & Sant'Anna 2024).
  - No anticipation.
  - SUTVA / no interference.
  - Correct cell classification via the nonresident rate.
- Testable: realized-dose ES passes at the muni level (Wald p ~0.33, pre-property spec; re-check).
- Under strong parallel trends the estimates trace a single ACRT curve.

## The identification strategy

- Source of variation: the binding decomposition.
  - Inc-bind: increase moves the bill.
  - Inc-becomes: increase newly crosses the threshold.
  - Inc-nobind: increase does not move the bill — the placebo.
  - Dec mirrors not estimated (5/3/11 munis; fail parallel trends).
- Design: continuous stacked DiD; never-changers as controls; dose enters linearly.
- FE and clustering: muni-by-stack + year-by-stack; clustered by muni.

Model 1 — pooled, one coefficient per rate-setter:

\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
Y_{\tilde i \tilde t} = \alpha_{\tilde i} + \gamma_{\tilde t}
&+ \beta^{M}_{\text{Inc}}\,\Delta\tau^{M}_{it}\,\mathbf{1}\{d^{M}_{i} = \text{Inc}\} \\
&+ \beta^{SD}_{\text{Inc}}\,\Delta\tau^{SD}_{it}\,\mathbf{1}\{d^{SD}_{i} = \text{Inc}\} \\
&+ \mathbf{X}'_{it}\boldsymbol{\phi} + \varepsilon_{\tilde i \tilde t}.
\end{split}
\label{eq:pooled}
\end{equation}

Model 2 — decomposition, one coefficient per binding cell (the headline):

\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
Y_{\tilde{i}\tilde{t}} = \alpha_{\tilde{i}} + \gamma_{\tilde{t}}
&+ \sum_{k \in \mathcal{C}_{-\text{NC}}} \beta^{\text{muni}}_k\,\Delta\tau^{\text{muni}}_{it}\,\mathbf{1}\{\text{cell}^{\text{muni}}_i = k\} \\
&+ \sum_{k \in \mathcal{C}_{-\text{NC}}} \beta^{\text{SD}}_k\,\Delta\tau^{\text{SD}}_{it}\,\mathbf{1}\{\text{cell}^{\text{SD}}_i = k\} \\
&+ \mathbf{X}'_{it}\boldsymbol{\phi} + \varepsilon_{\tilde{i}\tilde{t}}.
\end{split}
\label{eq:headline}
\end{equation}

Variables:

- $Y_{\tilde i \tilde t}$: outcome.
- $\tilde i, \tilde t$: muni and year within a cohort-stack.
- $\alpha_{\tilde i}, \gamma_{\tilde t}$: muni-by-stack and year-by-stack FE.
- $\Delta\tau^{M}_{it}, \Delta\tau^{SD}_{it}$: cumulative rate change since baseline (the dose); 0 for never-changers.
- $\mathbf{1}\{d^{M}_i = \text{Inc}\}$: increaser indicator.
- $\text{cell}_i \in \mathcal{C}_{-\text{NC}} = \{\text{Inc-bind}, \text{Inc-becomes}, \text{Inc-nobind}\}$; NC omitted.
- $\beta^{M}_{\text{Inc-bind}}$: the headline. $\beta^{M}_{\text{Inc-nobind}}$: the placebo.
- $\mathbf{X}_{it}$: spending shares + property effective rates.
- SEs clustered by muni.

Model 3 — realized-dose event study:

\begin{equation}
Y_{\tilde i \tilde t} = \alpha_{\tilde i} + \gamma_{\tilde t}
+ \sum_{k \neq -1} \beta^M_k\, \mathbf{1}\{\ell_{it} = k\}\,
\widetilde{D}_i
+ \mathbf{X}'_{it}\boldsymbol{\phi} + \varepsilon_{\tilde i \tilde t}.
\label{eq:realized-dose-es}
\end{equation}

- $\ell_{it}$: event time; window -5 to +5, k = -1 omitted.
- $\widetilde{D}_i$: realized dose at +5, constant per muni; 0 for never-changers.
- $\beta^M_k$: per-pp effect at k. Leads test strong parallel trends (Wald); lags trace dynamics.
- Run per cell on {cell, never-changers}; SD and nonresident cell x dose controls as in Model 2.

- Dose-response figures: spline version of these models, for visualization only; spec in Appendix.
- Threats: pre-trends (Model 3); property burden (controlled); functional form and weighting (Robustness).

# Robustness

1. Alternative estimator — dCDH (de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille 2024, non-negative weights).

   The building block is a switcher vs not-yet-switcher (should be never switchers) long difference at horizon $\ell$:

   \begin{equation}
   \widehat{DID}_{i,\ell} = \big(Y_{i,F_i+\ell} - Y_{i,F_i-1}\big) - \big(\bar Y^{c}_{F_i+\ell} - \bar Y^{c}_{F_i-1}\big)
   \label{eq:dcdh}
   \end{equation}

   - $F_i$: the year muni $i$ first changes its rate.
   - $\bar Y^{c}$: mean outcome among controls — munis with the same baseline rate, not yet changed by $F_i+\ell$; the continuous option replaces exact matching with a polynomial in the baseline level.
   - $\delta_\ell$: the reported effect — $\widehat{DID}_{i,\ell}$ averaged across switchers with non-negative weights.

   Differs from Models 1–2:
   - treatment is the rate level, not the cumulative dose;
   - baseline-level polynomial for conditional parallel trends;
   - per-event level effect, not a per-pp slope;
   - scalar treatment — cannot see the binding cell.
   - Results table like the main model:
     1. pooled dCDH (headline outcome), with ES figure for pre-trends.
     2. dCDH by cell (Inc-bind, Inc-becomes, Inc-nobind, headline outcome), with ES figure for pre-trends.
   - Say: sign and pre-trends reproduced everywhere; magnitudes reconcile (pooled, Inc-becomes) after rescaling; Inc-bind attenuates (discrete rule).
   - Note (the reconciliation logic — this is what rules out negative weighting):
     - $\delta_\ell$ is a level effect at the realized dose; the comparable feols quantity is ACR x mean dose (~0.33 pp), not the ACR itself.
     - Rescaled, pooled and Inc-becomes land on the dCDH numbers (e.g. Inc-becomes in-commuters: -0.247 x 0.381 = -0.094 vs dCDH -0.096). The residual pooled gap is horizon — dCDH stops at +3 while the dose accrues toward +5.
     - Inc-bind stays attenuated even rescaled (-0.007 vs expected -0.13): the binding cell is a discrete rule ($\tau^M+\tau^{SD}>\tau^{nr}$) the scalar treatment cannot see. The apparent Inc-bind/Inc-becomes ordering reversal is this attenuation, not a real reversal.
     - Since the non-negative-weight estimator reproduces the rescaled feols magnitudes where it can see the treatment, the linear ACR is not a negative-weighting artifact.

2. pre/post Act 32 — testing enforcement strength.

3. Act 47 — drop all Act 47 cities.

4. Pre-trend battery — four tests per cell (joint Wald, individual leads, linear pre-slope, HonestDiD breakdown); robust_clean verdict. Moved into the robustness script.

5. Dose-permutation randomization inference — shuffle dose magnitudes across treated munis, 500 draws; Inc-bind permutation p = 0.016 (dose size drives the result); Inc-becomes uninformative (identified off crossing, not size).

6. Fake-timing placebo — events shifted 4 years early, pre-event data only; Inc-bind null on all outcomes; Inc-becomes fails the counts (confirms its suggestive label).

# Discussion

- Compare magnitudes and signs to the sorting and local-tax literature.
- Mechanism: the EIT follows the worker; the property tax capitalizes into the parcel. Residence-based taxes sort, parcel-based taxes do not.
- The binding cell isolates the bill — not correlates of raising the rate.
- Policy: sorting erodes the base; matters for revenue forecasting and tax competition.
- Limits: PA's rule and withholding regime; identified off rate-changers; high-dose imprecise.

# Conclusion

- Restate: binding increases move workers; non-binding increases do not.
- The one thing it changes: residence-based local taxes carry a sorting cost parcel-based taxes do not — big enough to matter for revenue, not to reverse it.

# Appendix {.appendix}

## Spline specification (dose-response figures)

- The dose-response figures replace the linear dose with a natural cubic spline — visualization, not estimation; reported estimates are the linear ACR.

Pooled — muni and SD doses each get a spline:

$$Y_{\tilde i \tilde t} = \alpha_{\tilde i} + \gamma_{\tilde t} + \sum_j b^{M}_j\, s_j(\Delta\tau^{M}_{it}) + \sum_j b^{SD}_j\, s_j(\Delta\tau^{SD}_{it}) + \mathbf{X}'_{it}\boldsymbol{\phi} + \varepsilon_{\tilde i \tilde t}$$

Decomposition — per cell $k$ on {cell $k$, never-changers}, same splines (the subset replaces a cell-interacted spline, which would absorb the level):

$$Y_{\tilde i \tilde t} = \alpha_{\tilde i} + \gamma_{\tilde t} + \sum_j b^{M,k}_j\, s_j(\Delta\tau^{M}_{it}) + \sum_j b^{SD,k}_j\, s_j(\Delta\tau^{SD}_{it}) + \mathbf{X}'_{it}\boldsymbol{\phi} + \varepsilon_{\tilde i \tilde t}$$

- $s_j$: natural-spline basis; knots at dose terciles; linear beyond the boundary knots.
- $b_j$: basis coefficients. $\mathrm{ATT}(d)=\sum_j b_j[s_j(d)-s_j(0)]$; $\mathrm{ACRT}(d)=d\,\mathrm{ATT}/dd$.
- All other variables as in Models 1–2.
- BIC selects linear; the spline is for visuals.
- Full 8-panel figures: `acr_acrt_att_spline_pooled`, `_incbind`, `_incbecomes`.
- Note: code currently nets SD out linearly; SD-spline upgrade queued.
